intro: A biography of Elena Vidal, an invented botanist who spent her life studying plants. All the past tenses at work.
p.nacer.consejo: It is irregular: «nazco», «nací». You say «nació en Valencia». The c sounds th: «na-THER».
p.costurera.consejo: It comes from «coser». The masculine is «costurero» or «sastre».
p.licenciarse.consejo: You say «licenciarse en» a subject: «se licenció en Biología». It is pronominal.
p.directora.consejo: The masculine is «director». It ends in «-dora» in the feminine, like «profesora».
p.herbario.consejo: The h is silent: «er-BA-ryo». It keeps dried, ordered plants to study them.
p.defender.consejo: It changes e to ie: «defiendo». After «defender que» in the past comes the subjunctive: «pudieran».
p.aprobar.consejo: It changes o to ue: «apruebo». You approve a project or pass an exam.
p.mudarse.consejo: It is pronominal and takes «a»: «se mudó a Suiza». Not to be confused with «mudar», to change.
p.humilde.consejo: It is written with a silent initial h: «u-MIL-de». It applies to people and to families.
p.negarse.consejo: It is pronominal and takes «a»: «se negó a esperar». It changes e to ie: «me niego».
p.fallecer.consejo: It is the formal way of saying «morir». It is used in biographies and news: «falleció en 1972».
p.jubilarse.consejo: It is pronominal: «se jubiló». The j sounds like a strong h: «hu-bi-LAR-se».
p.jardín botánico.consejo: It is a scientific garden with plants from all over the world, each with its name.
b1.texto:
- The **indefinido** carries the milestones: **nació**, **se licenció**, **falleció**.
- The **imperfecto** gives the background to one of them: cuando **tenía** diez años…
- The **passive** fits public events: **fue nombrada**, **fue aprobado**.
- What someone argued for or asked for goes in the **past subjunctive**: defendió que los visitantes **pudieran** tocar las plantas; le pidieron que **esperara**.
- A **compound infinitive** looks back: sin **haber podido** volver.

Useful biography words: **nacer**, **criarse**, **licenciarse**, **casarse**, **trasladarse**, **fallecer**; **a los** treinta años; **en** 1931; **tras** la jubilación; **al** cerrarse el jardín.
b2.f0.texto: Elena Vidal was born in Valencia in 1888.
b2.f2.texto: When her father died, she left school and started working.
b2.f3.texto: She was a seamstress before going back to study.
b2.f4.texto: She graduated in Biology at the age of thirty-six.
b2.f5.texto: Later they appointed her director of the botanical garden.
b2.f6.texto: She argued that visitors should be able to touch the plants.
b2.f7.texto: Many colleagues asked her to wait.
b4.titulo: Indefinido, imperfect and passive in a life
b4.texto:
**Milestone → indefinido**: Elena **nació** en Valencia. **Se licenció** en Biología. **Falleció** en 1972.

**Background → imperfect**: cuando **tenía** diez años, murió su padre. «Tenía» is the background; «murió», the milestone.

**Public event → passive with ser**: el proyecto **fue aprobado** en 1931; ella **fue nombrada** directora.

**Request or defence → past subjunctive**: **le pidieron que esperara**; **defendió que pudieran** tocar las plantas.

**Dates**: **en** 1931; **en** octubre de 1931; **el** 1 de octubre; **a los** treinta años.
b4.e0.texto: Elena was born in Valencia into a modest family.
b4.e1.texto: When she was ten, her father died.
b4.e2.texto: The project was approved in October 1931.
b5.f0.texto: The botanical garden wakes early among vapours of dew.
b5.f1.texto: The gravel paths crunch under the steps of the first visitors.
b5.f2.texto: A girl touches a velvety leaf with her fingertips.
b5.f3.texto: The leaf trembles for a moment and gives back a shining drop.
b5.f4.texto: In the air floats a scent of damp earth and fresh mint.
b5.f5.texto: In the herbarium, the dried plants rest between sheets of yellow paper.
b5.f6.texto: Each one keeps a name written in an elegant, old-fashioned hand.
b5.f7.texto: A bronze plaque remembers the woman who created that place.
b5.f8.texto: The visitors stop for a moment in front of her portrait.
b5.f9.texto: Afterwards they follow the path with a new calm in their eyes.
b6.o0: Murió su padre y tuvo que trabajar
b6.o0.refuerzo: That is it: the text tells it that way.
b6.o1.refuerzo: The reason is not exams: it is a family event.
b6.o2: Su familia se mudó al extranjero
b6.o2.refuerzo: The text does not tell of a move; it tells of her father's death.
b6.pregunta: Why did she have to leave school?
b7.frase: Se licenció ____ los treinta y seis años.
b7.o0.refuerzo: Well done: age is said «a los… años».
b7.o1.refuerzo: «En» is not used for an age.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «De» is not used for an age.
b8.o0.refuerzo: They did not ask her to resign.
b8.o1.refuerzo: That is it: «le pidieron que esperara».
b8.o2.refuerzo: They did not ask her to change plan.
b8.pregunta: What did many colleagues ask her to do?
b9.frase: Defendió que los visitantes ____ tocar las plantas.
b9.o0.refuerzo: A real fact would take the indicative; here it is an idea argued for.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The conditional does not work after «defendió que».
b9.o2.refuerzo: That is it: what is argued for takes the subjunctive.
b9.pregunta: Which form follows «defendió que» in the past?
b10.o0.refuerzo: That is it: «tenía» describes the background situation.
b10.o2.refuerzo: It is a past, not a future.
b10.pregunta: In «cuando tenía diez años», which tense gives the background?
b11.frase: El proyecto del herbario fue aprobado en 1931
b11.traduccion: The herbarium project was approved in 1931
p.licenció.consejo: From «licencia», licence. The accent on the «ó» marks the past tense for «él» or «ella».
p.nombraron.consejo: From «nombre», name. Here it means to choose someone for a position.
p.defendió.consejo: From «defender», to defend. The «ie» in «defender» becomes «ió» in the past, stressed on «DYO».
p.pudieran.consejo: From «poder», to be able. It is in the subjunctive past, after an idea of wanting or asking.
p.tocar.consejo: The «c» before «a» is always «k». The infinitive ends in «-ar», the regular verb pattern.
p.esperara.consejo: From «esperar», to wait. This subjunctive form appears after a phrase that expresses a wish.
p.negó.consejo: From «negar», to deny. The accent on the «ó» marks the past tense for «ella».
p.octubre.consejo: The months in Spanish are written in lowercase. The «c» before «t» is a «k» sound.
p.vapores.consejo: Plural of «vapor». The «v» sounds like «b», and the stress falls on «PO».
p.rocío.consejo: Morning drops of water on plants. The «í» has a tilde, so the two vowels separate.
p.senderos.consejo: Plural of «sendero», a narrow path. The stress falls on «DE».
p.grava.consejo: Small stones used on paths. The «v» sounds like «b» in Spanish.
p.crujen.consejo: From «crujir», to crack or crunch. The «j» is pronounced «h».
p.aterciopelada.consejo: From «terciopelo», velvet. The feminine «-a» agrees with «hoja», which is feminine.
p.gota.consejo: A small amount of liquid, like a drop of water. The «g» before «o» is hard.
p.menta.consejo: A herb with a fresh smell, used in teas and drinks. The stress falls on «MEN».
p.bronce.consejo: A metal alloy, often used for statues. The «c» before «e» sounds like «th» in Spain.
p.creó.consejo: The past of «crear», to create. The accent on the «ó» shows the stress.
p.detienen.consejo: From «tener», to have, with «de-» meaning stop. The «ie» forms a diphthong «tye».
p.siguen.consejo: From «seguir», to follow or continue. The «gu» before «e» is a silent «u», so «SI-gen».
